sections.h2: Where is Clovis, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Clovis is the county seat of Curry County, on the Llano Estacado in eastern New Mexico, close to the Texas line. Wikipedia lists the city at 38,567 residents in the 2020 census and about 23.8 square miles of area.

Three highways, US 60, US 70 and US 84, run through town. US 60 and 84 lead west about 60 miles to Fort Sumner, US 70 runs southwest about 19 miles to Portales, and the three roads head east together to the state line at Texico and Farwell, Texas. Cannon Air Force Base sits roughly 7 to 8 miles west of the city center.

The town began in 1906 when the Santa Fe railway looked for the first level section of land west of Texico for a town site. The railroad put town lots on sale on May 1, 1907, and Clovis incorporated in 1909. The early name was Riley's Switch. That railroad origin continues: BNSF still runs a division point and a large freight yard in Clovis.

sections.h2: What drives the Clovis economy, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Four things carry most of the local economy: Cannon Air Force Base, the BNSF rail yard, agriculture and dairy processing, and a small group of manufacturers. When one of them shifts, house sales in Clovis tend to feel it.

Cannon is the largest single factor. The Air Force fact sheet for the 27th Special Operations Wing says about 6,500 military and civilian personnel work at Cannon and the nearby Melrose Air Force Range. It also describes a base population of more than 7,800 military personnel, civilian employees and family members, plus about 4,000 retirees. Military families move on assignment cycles, so a sale tied to a permanent change of station often runs on a fixed calendar.

The farm economy sits behind the town. Wikipedia describes peanut and cotton farming, cattle ranching and dairy, and notes that the Southwest Cheese plant between Clovis and Portales processes more than 2.3 billion pounds of milk a year. Clovis Municipal Airport has daily service to Denver on Key Lime Air.

  • Cannon Air Force Base and the 27th Special Operations Wing
  • BNSF Railway freight yard and dispatching
  • Dairy, peanut, cotton and cattle operations
  • Locally owned businesses downtown and along the highway corridors

sections.h2: What should a Clovis seller know about wind, hail, snow and tornadoes?
sections.html:
Clovis has a semi-arid climate with wind as the constant, and Wikipedia notes the city sits on the southern edge of Tornado Alley. Gusts regularly rise above 30 miles per hour, and the average wind speed is about 12 miles per hour across the flat, open land.

Spring brings frequent severe thunderstorms, and summer evenings bring heavy rain. Winter snow tends to arrive for several weeks in January and February. The same source says the town has almost no storm runoff system, so snowmelt and heavy rain can cause minor street flooding. If your lot is low or your garage floor sits near the street, buyers and inspectors will ask about it.

What that means for the house itself:

  • Roofs face wind and storm exposure all year. A buyer who finances may ask for lifted flashing, missing shingles or old patches to be fixed before closing.
  • Heating and cooling both matter here. The 1991 to 2020 normals show a January daily low near 22 degrees and a July daily high near 91 degrees, so buyers look at both systems.
  • Fences, sheds and carports can be damaged by wind. Note any repairs you have made.

A cash buyer prices these items into the offer and skips the repair negotiation. A listed sale usually does not.

sections.h2: What do Curry County property taxes look like for a Clovis house?
sections.html:
Curry County bills property tax in two halves, with the first half due November 10 and the second due April 10. The Treasurer's Office says bills go out on or before November 1, and at least half must be paid by December 10 to avoid interest and penalty.

The Assessor's Office values about 27,000 parcels of real property in the county. Taxable value is 33.33 percent of appraised value minus exemptions. Curry County is divided into four school and tax districts: Clovis, Texico, Melrose and Grady, so the school district that serves your address affects the rate on your bill.

Taxes unpaid for more than three years can lead to transfer of the property to the State of New Mexico and sale at public auction, according to the Treasurer. If you owe back taxes on a house you want to sell, raise it early with your title company, since a lien will have to be paid at closing.

sections.h2: How does a sale change the tax value of a Clovis home?
sections.html:
When a Clovis house sells, the county can reset its taxable value to current market value, which often raises the bill for the next owner. New Mexico statute 7-36-21.2 limits yearly increases on residential property to 3 percent over the prior year, or 6.1 percent over two years, whichever is higher. That limit does not apply in a tax year that follows a change of ownership.

The statute lists transfers that do not count as a change of ownership, such as certain transfers between spouses, to a child who lives in the home, or into a revocable trust. A sale to a buyer is not one of them. A buyer comparing two Clovis houses should ask how long each owner has held the property, because a long-held house may carry a lower valuation than the price suggests.

For sellers, the practical point is timing. The county Treasurer's calendar sets January 1 as the valuation date for each tax year, and title companies commonly divide the year's tax between buyer and seller at closing. Ask for that split in writing. The Assessor's Office also takes a Real Property Transfer Declaration Affidavit, and you can ask the Deeds Specialist there what they need after a deed records.

sections.h2: What city rules apply when you sell a house in Clovis?
sections.html:
The city runs a 311 portal called Clovis NM Works for non-emergency problems, and neighbors can use it to report nuisances such as debris in alleys or overgrown lots. Reports can be anonymous and can include a photo.

If you have an inherited or vacant house, check that no open complaint is attached to the address before you list. Building Safety and Code Compliance sit under the same city department, and online permitting is available through the city's permit portal. A deck, roof or electrical job done without a permit can slow a conventional sale, since a buyer's lender or inspector may ask for records.

Utilities are split by provider. The city site points water leaks to Epcor Water and power outages to Xcel Energy. Collect final readings on closing day so the buyer starts clean.

  • Pull your recent tax bill from the Curry County Treasurer, 417 Gidding Street, Suite 150.
  • Check the city code on Municode for yard, junk vehicle and structure rules.
  • Gather permit records for any work after you bought the house.
  • Ask your title company about unpaid tax or utility balances.

sections.h2: Who buys houses in Clovis, and which sale route fits which situation?
sections.html:
Buyers in Clovis fall into three groups: military households, local families, and investors who rent to both. Each group wants something different from a listing.

A military buyer using a VA loan faces an appraisal and condition review, which can be harder for a house with a failing roof or foundation movement. A local family may rely on a bank loan and a standard inspection. An investor or cash buyer can close on a shorter timeline and accept the house in its present state.

Selling on the open market can bring the highest price for a clean, updated house, but it also brings showings, inspection requests, appraisal risk and agent commission. A cash sale trades some of that price for speed and certainty. A direct sale suits a seller facing probate, a move on orders, tax debt, a tenant who will not leave, or repairs the family cannot pay for.

Whichever route you choose, ask for the offer in writing, ask who pays each closing cost, and have a New Mexico title company handle the closing. We do not promise a price here, since any figure depends on the house, the location and the work it needs.

faqs.q: How long does a cash sale take in Clovis?
faqs.a: It depends on title work, not on the buyer's financing. A clean title can close in a matter of weeks, while liens, probate or missing signatures add time. Your title company will give you a closing date once the file is opened.

faqs.q: Do I owe Curry County property tax when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes, for any tax year you owned the house on January 1 and any unpaid balance. Title companies usually collect the unpaid amount at closing, and the Treasurer's Office can confirm what is owed. First-half taxes are due November 10 and second-half taxes April 10.

faqs.q: Does a Clovis sale raise the property tax for the buyer?
faqs.a: Often yes. State law limits yearly increases to 3 percent for residential property, but that limit does not apply in the tax year after a change of ownership, so the county can value the house at current market value.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Clovis house that needs a new roof?
faqs.a: Yes. Wind and storm damage are common on the plains, and a cash buyer will usually take the house as it stands and price the roof into the offer. A bank-financed buyer may ask for the roof to be fixed first.

faqs.q: What if the house is inherited and still in a parent's name?
faqs.a: You will need legal authority to sell, which usually means probate or a court-approved personal representative in New Mexico. Talk to a New Mexico attorney first, then ask the title company what documents it needs.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a nuisance complaint on my Clovis property?
faqs.a: The city accepts reports through its Clovis NM Works 311 portal and handles code questions through Building Safety and Code Compliance. Clearing the issue before you sell avoids delays at closing.
